_readme: Third-party skills vendored into the shipped tree, with provenance and licence.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `.claude/skills` is a directory junction pointing at this
tree (see scripts/sync_skills.py), so local Claude Code and VOLT read the same
files and cannot drift. The cost of that convenience is that `npx skills add X`
or `npx skillfish add X` writes STRAIGHT INTO the client-facing corpus.
tests/test_skill_provenance.py fails if a skill directory appears here that is
not listed below and not VOLT-authored. That turns a silent corpus pollution
into a loud CI failure, and forces the licence check that `lev-os/agents` failed
(no LICENSE file at all -- all rights reserved -- so nothing from it is vendored).
TO ADD A THIRD-PARTY SKILL: confirm the licence permits redistribution, copy the
directory in, add an entry here, include the upstream LICENCE text alongside, and
measure retrieval before/after with scripts/measure_retrieval.py -- a new skill
that displaces a purpose-built VOLT skill is a regression, not an addition.

notes: Descriptions are YAML block scalars, so every one of these indexed as a
single '|' character until the parser fix in c3c9d47.
Retrieval measured before and after: 5 rank-1 corrections, 0 displacements
of a VOLT-authored skill. fair-value-hierarchy went from enterprise-value
0.102 to ifrs 0.268; FINTRAC-STR from llmquant-data 0.110 to str-report
0.148. revenue-recognition (0.492), lease-accounting (0.390) and
kyc-aml-financial-crime (0.213) all held rank 1 against the new skills.
These descriptions end with a 'not for X' exclusion list. TF-IDF cannot
represent negation, so those words match POSITIVELY. _MAX_DESCRIPTION=800
happens to truncate most of that tail. If the cap is ever raised, re-measure.
Requested as `/plugin install sap-fi@sapstack sap-session@sapstack`. A Claude
Code plugin installs into ~/.claude/plugins, which VOLT never reads, so the
plugin route would have changed nothing about a client answer. The skill
directory inside the plugin is what was vendored.
sap-fi is T-code-level SAP FI troubleshooting -- posting errors, GR/IR,
period/year-end close, asset accounting, tax config. Measured: sap-fi takes
rank 1 on 'GR/IR clearing account not clearing after MIRO posting' (0.267)
and 'SAP FI year-end close and asset depreciation run AFAB' (0.341), both of
which previously returned nothing relevant. No existing skill was displaced.
sap-session was requested and DELIBERATELY NOT VENDORED. It is a session-state
and evidence-bundle workflow tool, not domain content -- the same class as the
36 dev-workflow skills whose presence made `stress-test` outrank
banking-compliance on a bank capital question. Nothing in it would improve an
answer to a client; it would only compete for retrieval.
Deviation from upstream: the de/ja/ko/vi/zh reference directories were dropped
(SKILL.md and the English/neutral references are byte-identical). Only SKILL.md
feeds the index, so the translations were inert weight that could still surface
in a deliverable. Re-add them if a non-English engagement needs them.
The other 22 plugins in the repo (sap-co, sap-tr, sap-mm, sap-sd, sap-abap,
sap-s4-migration, ...) are the same shape and licence if a project needs them.
Each is ONE framework with a mandated output format, which is why they were
taken over the repo's three overlapping strategy-consultant variants and its
eight industry packs (edtech/fintech/saas/... -- none of our industries).
strategy-consultant-7 is the chained orchestrator over the other seven.
They do NOT replace management-consulting: that one carries the firm's exhibit
and citation conventions and the visual mapping. These carry the structuring
method, which the corpus described but never showed a required output shape for.
Retrieval measured over eight representative queries (IFRS 18, controllership TOM,
close root-cause, insource/outsource structuring, FT savings sizing, Oracle ERP-EPM,
IFRS 17 CSM, utilities RFP): 0 displacements at rank 1, and these surface only where
structuring IS the ask -- five-whys at rank 2 on 'why is close taking 12 days',
pyramid-principle at rank 5 on 'structure the question of whether to insource'.
scripts/measure_retrieval.py referenced above does not exist in this tree; measured
directly against api.graph.skill_index.retrieve_skills instead.
Adapted from web-interface-guidelines/command.md: the upstream rules are inlined into SKILL.md instead of
fetched at runtime, because VOLT chat cannot fetch URLs. Upstream lines are carried
verbatim; the frontmatter and the fetch instruction were replaced. Re-pull to update.
The commit is the last upstream change to command.md before the vendoring date.

rejected.reason: No LICENSE file in the repository (GitHub reports licence: null), so all rights are reserved and there is no grant to redistribute inside a commercial client deliverable.
rejected.content_quality: Good -- combined ratio decomposition, Schedule P triangles, risk-based capital, NPW/PHS leverage.
rejected.resolution: Not vendored. insurance-financial-analysis was written independently from the same public industry metrics and framed for Canadian regulation (OSFI MCT rather than US risk-based capital, IFRS 17 rather than US statutory accounting), which fits VOLT's client base better than the original.
